abstract: We propose a self-supervised approach for learning room impulse response (RIR) representations from single-channel noisy-reverberant speech. It consists of first training on reverberant data, then on noisy-reverberant data, and finally with a teacher-student approach, where the student learns to replicate the teacher's embeddings when given a noisy version of the reverberant input. We assess their representational capabilities by estimating acoustic room parameters from them. Conditioning a discriminative speech enhancement model on the derived embeddings yields consistent gains across all evaluated metrics, including downstream word error rate, for both reverberant and noisy-reverberant speech.

oneSentenceThesis: 针对单通道带噪混响语音中房间信息易被噪声掩盖的问题，论文采用纯混响对比学习、带噪混响对比学习、冻结教师对齐学生三阶段学出噪声鲁棒的房间嵌入，并以声学参数探针和条件化深滤波增强验证其可读性与一致增益，代价是弱识别器仍受增强伪影影响且动态多通道场景未验证。
originalTitle: Room Impulse Response Embeddings for Speech Enhancement in Noisy and Reverberant Environments
